c74object.name: evi_env
c74object.digest: A GenExpr file, part of 'evieve', for using via 'require()'
c74object.description:
evi_env.genexpr is a .genexpr file and is part of the 'evieve' Package.
It is for using in a gen.codebox~ or in another .genexpr file via the require() command.
By declaring require("evi_env.genexpr"); at the top of a codebox you can then access all of the functions included in this file.
About this File:
Envelope (following) routines.

entry.name: averageAbsolute ( )
entry.description:
Like MSP [average~ absolute]
In 1: type=input: inputSample, Audio input to follow
In 2: type=input: windowSizeInSamples, Averaging window size in samples
Return 1: Average, Envelope output

entry.name: averageCore ( )
entry.description:
Generalised for options, used by 'averageWrap()'
In 1: type=input: X, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: reset, Sample accurate reset of internal state
In 3: type=param (optional): windowSize, default: 0, Optional window size in samples, default 1000 samples (like MSP)
Return 1: Average, Mean average envelope output
Return 2: Count, Index count of window buffer in samples

entry.name: averageWrap ( )
entry.description:
This is expensive because it branches internally, but is useful if you need to switch averaging type
In 1: type=input: X, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: reset, Sample accurate reset of internal state
In 3: type=param (optional): interval, default: 500, Interval (window size) in samples
In 4: type=param (optional): mode, default: 0, 0=bipolar, 1=absolute, 2=rms
Return 1: Average, Mean average envelope output
Return 2: Count, Index count of window buffer in samples

entry.name: averageData ( )
entry.description:
Averaging audio detection wrapper for envelope following
In 1: type=input: xin, Audio input to be analysed
In 2: type=input: reset, Sample accurate reset of the averaging filter (buffer)
In 3: type=param (optional): interval, default: 200, Interval (window size) in samples of internal averager algorithm
Return 1: Fast, Fast response data (exp)

entry.name: envRawDetect ( )
entry.description:
Simple, cheap and raw envelope following, intended to be used with post envelope smoothers such as in 'envFollSimple()'
In 1: type=input: x, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: attack, Attack amount normalised 0..1
In 3: type=input: release, Release amount normalised 0..1
Return 1: Raw, Raw envelope values output

entry.name: envDecay ( )
entry.description:
Logarithmic decay envelope follower
In 1: type=input: x, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: d, Decay time in SECONDS (to drop 6dB)
Return 1: Env, Output Envelope

entry.name: envAttackDecay ( )
entry.description:
Logarithmic attack/decay envelope follower
In 1: type=input: x, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: a, Attack time in SECONDS (to drop 6dB)
In 3: type=input: d, Decay time in SECONDS (to drop 6dB)
In 4: type=input: r,
Return 1: Env, Output Envelope

entry.name: envAttackHoldRelease ( )
entry.description:
Logarithmic attack/hold/release envelope follower
In 1: type=input: x, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: a, Attack time in SECONDS (to drop 6dB)
In 3: type=input: h, Hold time in SECONDS
In 4: type=input: r, Release time in SECONDS (to drop 6dB)
Return 1: Env, Output Envelope

entry.name: immediateEnv ( )
entry.description:
Absolute audio envelope peak followed by logarithmic envelope follower
In 1: type=input: iX, Audio input to be followed
In 2: type=input: iAttack, Envelope follower attack time in seconds
In 3: type=input: iDecay, Envelope follower release time in seconds
In 4: type=input: iR, Sample accurate reset of internal envelope following filter
Return 1: Immediate Env, Envelope output

entry.name: zeroxEnvs ( )
entry.description:
Fast data, slow envelopes (output envelope averages lower if melodic / sustained input, spikes to higher floor if transient / constantly changing input)
In 1: type=input: X, Audio input to be analysed
In 2: type=input: smooth, Smoothing time of the logarithmic smoothers in milliseconds
In 3: type=input: reset, Sample accurate reset of internal zero crossing detector
In 4: type=param (optional): countDiv, default: 10, Divisor for number of zero crossings per period, higher values will result in less busy envelopes (effects 'Env 2' middle outlet)
Return 1: Env 1, Based on zero crossing threshold
Return 2: Env 2, Based on number of zero crossings per period
Return 3: Xings, Continuously updated number of zero crossings

entry.name: vactrol ( )
entry.description:
Vactrol time-domain behaviour filter, the resistive part of a photoresistive opto-isolator
In 1: type=input: impulse, Impulse
In 2: type=input: rise, Rise time in SAMPLES
In 3: type=input: fall, Fall time in SAMPLES
In 4: type=input: base, Base frequency in Hz, should be in range 100..10000; very powerful in changing shape of envelope curve and peak/trough of envelope.
In 5: type=input: reset, Sample accurate reset of internal envelope following filter
Return 1: Vactrol Envelope, Output will behave similarly to a Buchla vactrol

entry.name: envFollSimple ( )
entry.description:
Quick, simple, cheap
In 1: type=input: X, Value to follow
In 2: type=input: attack, Attack 0..1 represents 0..10 ms
In 3: type=input: release, Release 0..1 represents 0..100 ms
Return 1: Env, Output Envelope
